name: Judgment
definition: You look beyond short term fixes in favor of long term solutions; you make wise decisions despite ambiguity; you use data to inform your intuition.

rows.situation: A problem with a fast patch and a slower fix
rows.under: Ships the patch, closes the ticket, and leaves the same problem for next month.
rows.justRight: Uses the patch only to stop the bleeding, and schedules the fix that removes the cause.
rows.over: Refuses every short patch, including the one that keeps customers working while the long fix is built.

rows.situation: A decision the data will not settle this week
rows.under: Waits for certainty the calendar will not give you.
rows.justRight: Names what you know, what you are guessing, and decides. Writes down what would change your mind.
rows.over: Decides in the first ten minutes and treats later facts as a nuisance.

rows.situation: A hunch that the numbers can test
rows.under: Goes with the hunch and does not look at the numbers you already have.
rows.justRight: Lets the data inform the hunch. If the numbers disagree, you can say why you are still going, or you change the call.
rows.over: Will not move until a dashboard says yes, including when the dashboard does not measure the thing you are deciding.

rows.under: Looks only for evidence that supports it.
rows.justRight: Asks what would show the call is wrong, and gives that a real chance before you commit.
rows.over: Talks yourself out of every call by collecting objections until the window closes.

rows.situation: A decision in someone else's craft
rows.under: Overrules the person closest to the work because you are senior.
rows.justRight: Weights the judgment of the people whose craft this is, and says whose view carried the call.
rows.over: Defers every call to the nearest specialist and will not make one when the specialists disagree.
